A Marathon a day for 35 days

By: Julian Sun | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Running a marathon is hard enough... but what about 30 marathons in 35 days?

Unique Selling Point:
We look at the physical and mental toll a journey of this magnitude takes on the minds and bodies of lifelong friend Matt and Charles and they undertake the adventure of a lifetime. Will they make it all the way to Cape Town? and what price will they pay for daring to run such an arduous race?

Summary:
The “Running Wild” Fundraising Campaign is the initiative of Matthew Murray and Charles Raw. These adventure, running – and conservation enthusiasts have decided to do a mammoth run to help raise funds for Velakukhanya Primary School based in KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa. 

The pair will be running in South Africa from Port Alfred to Cape Town, spanning 1, 222 km in 35 consecutive days - just shy of a marathon each day! Charles and Matt chose Velakukhanya Primary School as a project in their beloved province of KwaZulu-Natal, where they want to make a difference to the KwaNgwenya community and to the learners at this school, who did not have the same opportunities as they had growing up. 

Matt and Charles began their epic quest at the beginning of February and are about halfway to achieving their goal. If all goes according to plan, they'll finish on the 7th March in Cape Town. They’re running around 42km per day and are already dealing with the stresses and strains of running a marathon a day. Pushing through the pain of blistered feet, strained achilles tendons, damaged knees and the physical and mental fatigue is the desire to raise R2.3 million for the school.

Script:


V/O: Anyone that’s run a 42km marathon knows the blood, sweat and tears that they’ve had to endure to make it to the finish line.

MAC (to camera): And then it’s the following day… blistering feet, painful knees and aching ankles. But at least you’ve got time to recover, right? Imagine having to do for another day and then the day after for a whole month… Who’d be crazy enough to attempt that?

V/O: Meet Matt Murray and Charles Raw, two childhood friends with a bold idea: run a marathon a day for 35 days to raise money for a worthy cause.

Matt (upsound): Hamstring’s gone!

Charlie(upsound): Quads are gone, we’ve only got 6 to go so…

V/O: Their adventure began on the 1st of February in Port Alfred in the Eastern Cape and culminated at the Beau Constantia Wine Farm in Cape Town.

V/O: Over the past month, the duo has trekked over 1200km, making new friends and unforgettable memories along the way…

Upsound (group of boys running): I wanna be a quester!

V/O: We caught up with them in the middle of their journey to delve into the heart and soul of this extraordinary feat of endurance.

Mac: You are?

Matt: Matt

Charles: Charles

Mac: Howzit boys, how are you doing?

Charles: Lekker and you

Mac: Lekker man, so you are the mad runners doing a marathon a day?

Charles: That’s us!

Mac: Why?! Why?!

Charles: There’s various answers to that, but it’s been a good journey so far, 28 days in, feeling strong.

V/O: Supporting them on the road are Charles’ wife Michaela and their two-year-old daughter Callie

Charlie to Callie (Upsound): Brush, Brush, Brush!

Michaela: So my job is basically to do the pictures and, like, the social media and stuff like that, and then take care of this little one, and then also keep the boys hydrated and fueled and stuff for the run.

Michaela: This time with her has been so special because there’s moments when it’s just her and I and like we sleep together in bed and that’s been really awesome

V/O: Today’s run ended in the town of Struisbaai. After 5 hours on the road, Matt and Charles returned to basecamp. Tired limbs and aching muscles were relieved in an ice bath.

Charles: Now it’s getting icy

Mac: Does it make you recover quicker? Does it take away the pain? Does it just make you cold?

Matt: I think the inflammation that the initial pain is the first trick. Yeah. Take that away. Inflammation a lot. Like I can't feel my hamstrings. My one. My one calf and hamstring was pretty, pretty bleak. Now it's a bit better.

V/O: Matt and Charles are from the KwaZulu-Natal midlands and have been friends since Grade 2. They bonded over a shared love of sport, be it on the cricket or rugby field and now the open road.

Matt: Through sport we've grown, mutual respect for, like, each other's capabilities. But sports can humble you. And so it comes with its highs and lows. And I think that's what you're experiencing on this trip as well, which is, which is sort of set us up for the success of getting through this without being at each other's necks and things

Mac: So whose crazy idea was it? Right. Boet, I'm going to go to 32 marathons in 32 days…

Charles: We were at a braai one afternoon and Matt and I follow quite a few of these mad men on social media. And we were chatting about it, and I said to him, why don't we take a week off work and do something similar? Run for a week, something along those lines and it's gone from a week to five weeks.

Matt: I was the one who said, let's do it for a reason. But if it's going to gain any sort of traction, it's going to be something that's hard. And that's where it became, well maybe we'll get to run a marathon, a day for a month.

V/O: And so the Running Wild Campaign was born, with an aim to raise R2.3 million for the children of Velakukhanya Primary School in northern KwaZulu-Natal.

Matt (upsound) Running with kids at the school: Go!

Charles: So for us to have the opportunity to provide a better education for these kids, better classrooms, I mean, that kitchen, I'll never forget it you know. It’s such a sad story.

Matt (Upsound): We’ve got the Knysna marathon running club with us. Look at this view!

Matt: We've had a lot of amazing support messages from people who've bought into this idea. And, had a look just before our interview and saw that we had reached R500,000 around today.

V/O: For the past month, people have followed their journey on social media. Initially things went smoothly, but after just a few days, a problem…

Matt (Upsound): Unfortunately I’ve got a searing pain in my achilles, everything else feels pretty good…

Matt: I remember just saying to Charlie, you'll like something's gone in this in this leg, and it felt like a red hot poker in my Achilles. I immediately couldn't run. Eventually I said to Charlie, listen, there's a chance I'm not finishing, so you need to carry the flag here pal.

Mac: Were you worried that you might have to end up finishing this race on your own?

Charles: It did cross my mind a few times. I mean, the man couldn't walk, so I was definitely thinking about that.

Matt: But I said, if I, if I do give up now, then I've given up on it that then it's done. Let me try to get through today and then let's reassess and so we walked through that day

V/O: Despite pushing ahead, it was clear: an intervention was needed. And so, their on-call podiatrist, Nelfrie Kemp was brought in.

Nelfrie: We had to do injury prevention because 35 days stopping is not an option. Resting is not an option. Recovery is not an option. We had to prep them as best as possible that they could last for 35 days.

Mac: What spurred you on to say “I want to go see what's going on”

Nelfrie: They were sore, they were worried. Matt went for a scan and they were worried that there was a muscle tear. I just knew I had to go there because I wanted to see for myself.

Matt (Upsound) while being treated by Nelfrie: I’m struggling to stand on that foot, hey.

Nelfrie (upsound) while treating Matt: I was very relieved that the scan said that it’s not torn

Matt (Upsound): Ja

Nelfrie: The cause of his calf pain was coming from the position of his foot and also the shoe that he was in. I massaged them, strapped them, stretched them, all of that. And then the next day he managed to walk. So we established that it’s not a tear through, through a scan. And then I knew that as long as I placed that foot in the correct position, we weren't going to strain that muscle more.

Charles: If we hadn't met Nelfrie when we did, we wouldn't be sitting here, she's been also a superhero. Just fortunate to meet you when we did. And it's crazy. She pulled in on the 8th of Feb. Matt was really struggling. He was up and running in, I think in 3 or 4 days after that.

V/O: Following her intervention, the guys made steady progress as they inched ever-closer to their destination. With the last leg of their journey ahead of them, Nelfrie returned for one final assessment..

Nelfrie (upsound): They’ve got about 8 days left so I definitely think the muscles need a good stretch

Nelfrie (upsound): Howzit guys!

Matt and Charles (upsound): Nelfrie!

Nelfrie (upsound): How are you?

Matt (upsound): Good and you?!

Nelfrie (upsound): How’s your muscles? When last did you have a massage?

Charles (Upsound): probably a week ago.


V/O: Having run almost 1000km, the guys were treated to their first massage in over a week.

Charles (Upsound): The left quad for the past 3 or 4 days has been quite painful.

V/O: That evening, everyone gathered for a home-cooked meal, courtesy of Michaela. 4 weeks into their journey, it’s things like this that helped keep up morale. After dinner it’s straight to bed before another early start.


V/O: 4am is the regular wake-up time for the guys. time to get dressed, strap up and prepare for the day’s run.

MAC to camera: So after spending the day with Matt and Charles yesterday, I’m inspired to join them for part of their 42km run. But it’s almost 4 o'clock in the morning… Nobody should be awake at this time!

V/O: But first, a 30km drive to the starting point in the village of Elim.

Charles (upsound): Today we’ve got a 40km day, we're starting in the small town of Elim and we’re gonna be running down to Gaansbaai

V/O: As they neared the finish in Gaansbaai, I joined them for the last few kms of the run

Mac (upsound): Listen boys, I know you’re trying to keep up… I’m super proud of you!

*Laughs*

V/O: Having run 30 marathons in 35 days, covering a total distance of 1244km, the idea of making it to the finish line stirred up some emotion.

Matt: I'm not an emotional oke, but I think I'm going to be emotional!

Charles: It's going to be unbelievable. if we can finish on the 7th of March in Cape Town, I think people will see what we've been through. What are we going to raise for that school and see what future we can bring for the kids, That's our main goal.


PROMO 1:
MAC: Two lifelong friends came up with an audacious idea to run 30 Marathons in a row.

MATT: Initially, it was let's take a week off in there for run and then I was the one who said, let's do it for a reason. But if it's going to gain any sort of traction, it's going to be something that's hard.

MAC: We look at the physical and mental toll that this will take on them.


PROMO 2:
MAC: Endurance is the ability to exert oneself and remain active for a long period of time.

MATT:It's when I'm struggling with big injuries, that's when you really delve into the Hurt Locker and getting through your day is, is long. You start to have self-doubt.

MAC: Two friends put this to the ultimate test as they attempt to run 30 marathons in just 35 days.


PROMO 3
V/O: Running a 42km marathon is hard! Now imagine running one a day, every day, for a whole month. That’s the challenge that two friends set themselves to raise money for a worthy cause.

Matt: I've thought a number of times on this trip, like, why, why did we decide that long, what was 40km a day? There's definitely been times we have questioned, why have we done this?

And, had a look just before our interview and saw that we had reached R500,000 around today. V/O: For the past month, people have followed their journey on social media. Initially things went smoothly, but after just a few days, a problem… Matt (Upsound): Unfortunately I’ve got a searing pain in my achilles, everything else feels pretty good… Matt: I remember just saying to Charlie, you'll like something's gone in this in this leg, and it felt like a red hot poker in my Achilles. I immediately couldn't run. Eventually I said to Charlie, listen, there's a chance I'm not finishing, so you need to carry the flag here pal. Mac: Were you worried that you might have to end up finishing this race on your own? Charles: It did cross my mind a few times. I mean, the man couldn't walk, so I was definitely thinking about that. Matt: But I said, if I, if I do give up now, then I've given up on it that then it's done. Let me try to get through today and then let's reassess and so we walked through that day V/O: Despite pushing ahead, it was clear: an intervention was needed. And so, their on-call podiatrist, Nelfrie Kemp was brought in. Nelfrie: We had to do injury prevention because 35 days stopping is not an option. Resting is not an option. Recovery is not an option. We had to prep them as best as possible that they could last for 35 days. Mac: What spurred you on to say “I want to go see what's going on” Nelfrie: They were sore, they were worried. Matt went for a scan and they were worried that there was a muscle tear. I just knew I had to go there because I wanted to see for myself. Matt (Upsound) while being treated by Nelfrie: I’m struggling to stand on that foot, hey. Nelfrie (upsound) while treating Matt: I was very relieved that the scan said that it’s not torn Matt (Upsound): Ja Nelfrie: The cause of his calf pain was coming from the position of his foot and also the shoe that he was in. I massaged them, strapped them, stretched them, all of that. And then the next day he managed to walk. So we established that it’s not a tear through, through a scan. And then I knew that as long as I placed that foot in the correct position, we weren't going to strain that muscle more. Charles: If we hadn't met Nelfrie when we did, we wouldn't be sitting here, she's been also a superhero. Just fortunate to meet you when we did. And it's crazy. She pulled in on the 8th of Feb. Matt was really struggling. He was up and running in, I think in 3 or 4 days after that. V/O: Following her intervention, the guys made steady progress as they inched ever-closer to their destination. With the last leg of their journey ahead of them, Nelfrie returned for one final assessment.. Nelfrie (upsound): They’ve got about 8 days left so I definitely think the muscles need a good stretch Nelfrie (upsound): Howzit guys! Matt and Charles (upsound): Nelfrie! Nelfrie (upsound): How are you? Matt (upsound): Good and you?! Nelfrie (upsound): How’s your muscles? When last did you have a massage? Charles (Upsound): probably a week ago. V/O: Having run almost 1000km, the guys were treated to their first massage in over a week. Charles (Upsound): The left quad for the past 3 or 4 days has been quite painful. V/O: That evening, everyone gathered for a home-cooked meal, courtesy of Michaela. 4 weeks into their journey, it’s things like this that helped keep up morale. After dinner it’s straight to bed before another early start. V/O: 4am is the regular wake-up time for the guys. time to get dressed, strap up and prepare for the day’s run. MAC to camera: So after spending the day with Matt and Charles yesterday, I’m inspired to join them for part of their 42km run. But it’s almost 4 o'clock in the morning… Nobody should be awake at this time! V/O: But first, a 30km drive to the starting point in the village of Elim. Charles (upsound): Today we’ve got a 40km day, we're starting in the small town of Elim and we’re gonna be running down to Gaansbaai V/O: As they neared the finish in Gaansbaai, I joined them for the last few kms of the run Mac (upsound): Listen boys, I know you’re trying to keep up… I’m super proud of you! *Laughs* V/O: Having run 30 marathons in 35 days, covering a total distance of 1244km, the idea of making it to the finish line stirred up some emotion. Matt: I'm not an emotional oke, but I think I'm going to be emotional! Charles: It's going to be unbelievable. if we can finish on the 7th of March in Cape Town, I think people will see what we've been through. What are we going to raise for that school and see what future we can bring for the kids, That's our main goal. PROMO 1: MAC: Two lifelong friends came up with an audacious idea to run 30 Marathons in a row. MATT: Initially, it was let's take a week off in there for run and then I was the one who said, let's do it for a reason. But if it's going to gain any sort of traction, it's going to be something that's hard. MAC: We look at the physical and mental toll that this will take on them. PROMO 2: MAC: Endurance is the ability to exert oneself and remain active for a long period of time. MATT:It's when I'm struggling with big injuries, that's when you really delve into the Hurt Locker and getting through your day is, is long. You start to have self-doubt. MAC: Two friends put this to the ultimate test as they attempt to run 30 marathons in just 35 days. PROMO 3 V/O: Running a 42km marathon is hard! Now imagine running one a day, every day, for a whole month. That’s the challenge that two friends set themselves to raise money for a worthy cause. Matt: I've thought a number of times on this trip, like, why, why did we decide that long, what was 40km a day? There's definitely been times we have questioned, why have we done this?

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Running a marathon is hard enough... but what about 30 marathons in 35 days?
metadata.Unique Selling Point: We look at the physical and mental toll a journey of this magnitude takes on the minds and bodies of lifelong friend Matt and Charles and they undertake the adventure of a lifetime. Will they make it all the way to Cape Town? and what price will they pay for daring to run such an arduous race?
metadata.Summary: The “Running Wild” Fundraising Campaign is the initiative of Matthew Murray and Charles Raw. These adventure, running – and conservation enthusiasts have decided to do a mammoth run to help raise funds for Velakukhanya Primary School based in KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa. The pair will be running in South Africa from Port Alfred to Cape Town, spanning 1, 222 km in 35 consecutive days - just shy of a marathon each day! Charles and Matt chose Velakukhanya Primary School as a project in their beloved province of KwaZulu-Natal, where they want to make a difference to the KwaNgwenya community and to the learners at this school, who did not have the same opportunities as they had growing up. Matt and Charles began their epic quest at the beginning of February and are about halfway to achieving their goal. If all goes according to plan, they'll finish on the 7th March in Cape Town. They’re running around 42km per day and are already dealing with the stresses and strains of running a marathon a day. Pushing through the pain of blistered feet, strained achilles tendons, damaged knees and the physical and mental fatigue is the desire to raise R2.3 million for the school.
